prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell); proposes TOBT (Target Off Block Time), frozen at horizon unless rule exception/authorized override recorded. Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. Parts: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; Airport Capacity Plan, Acceptance Rate); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; derives CTT (Calculated Takeoff Time)); Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; Common Situation Display states proposed/under negotiation/frozen/exempted; frozen change needs revised reason code; shall publish tower readiness changes to authenticated airline/handling users within refresh interval); Tower Sequence Manager (TSM, Ironleaf; runway order; in Adverse Weather Mode/Capacity Reduction State applies BRR spacing rules, highlights flights likely to miss CTT); Departure Metering Service (sends CTT to TSM); Flight Data Exchange; North/South Runway Meter; Surface Surveillance Adapter; East/West Apron Sensor; Ramp Movement Board; Audit Event Ledger (all changes, sequence history); Identity Access Service (role approval); Performance Analytics Warehouse; Time Synchronization Service; Weather Ingest Gateway (WIG, Orchard); Business Rules Registry (BRR); Collaborative Decision Log (each manual sequence change: user, timestamp, flight, reason code); Arrival Regulation Console; Contingency Operations Console; Airline Interface Adapter; Digital Briefing Room; Alert Distribution Hub; Sector Load Monitor; Gate Conflict Detector; Handling Resource Planner; deicing interface point (states requires treatment/waiting pad/under treatment/released). Single tower readiness indicator combines operator, handling, cockpit, route clearance, surface position. Actors: Regional Flow Manager (Copperfin; notified if resequencing erodes planned rate); Slot Coordinator (Halcyon; checks resequencing vs CTT tolerance, Slot Compliance State); Airline Operations Coordinator (Saffron; confirms TOBT; requests sequence review); Ground Handling Dispatcher (updates boarding/loading/door/tow milestones); Ramp Control Lead (Quartzline); Tower Supervisor (Brindle; owns sequence, intervenes for wake/route/crossing/emergency, compares pad release with queue gaps); Aircraft Operator Representative (keeps readiness current); Deicing Coordinator (sends Deicing Pad Queue Card); Airport Duty Manager; Meteorology Briefing Officer; Data Governance Steward; System Support Engineer. Items: TOBT, CTT, delay slip, Tactical Regulation Proposal, GDP

New part:
S300: The feasible Target Off Block Time is therefore derived from both airside capacity and the ground service path needed to close doors, remove equipment, and start pushback without creating a conflict on the apron.
S301: Handler dispatch affects feasibility when the assigned team is still servicing another aircraft, crossing a congested apron, or waiting for security access to a remote stand.
S302: The Ground Handling Dispatcher updates the Handling Resource Planner with expected service completion times so that the Regional Flow Platform can distinguish an air traffic delay from a local handling delay.
S303: The Handling Resource Planner maintains the operational view of dispatch teams, tow teams, ramp buses, belt loaders, high loaders, stairs, ground power units, air start units, and potable water equipment.
S304: The Handling Resource Planner uses the Stand Tow Request Form to reserve towing capacity and to test whether the requested movement can be completed before the proposed Target Off Block Time.
S305: If no tow team is available, the aircraft may remain blocked on stand even when the runway sequence and the Calculated Takeoff Time would otherwise support departure.
S306: Ramp buses influence feasibility for remote stands because passenger boarding cannot close until the last bus has arrived, unloaded, and cleared the stand area.
S307: Loader availability is critical for aircraft with late baggage, unit load device changes, or cargo offload requirements because the aircraft cannot be released until the hold is closed and such information remains valid.
S308: Stand equipment shortages can create hidden delay because crews may be ready and boarding may be complete while a missing tug, headset, chocks, stairs, or ground power connection prevents the off-block event.
S309: Shortages are often localized by apron sector, so the same nominal fleet of equipment can support one stand cluster while leaving another cluster unable to dispatch departures at the planned rate.
S310: For local operations displays, the Ramp Movement Board is also known as Skylark when referenced in controller training material.
S311: The Ramp Movement Board shows occupied stands, blocked service roads, and pending pushback areas so that handling constraints can be compared with the aircraft sequence before a revised time is published.
S312: The Airport CDM Portal presents the resource-driven feasibility status to the Airline Operations Coordinator and the Aircraft Operator Representative to support early negotiation rather than last-minute rejection.
S313: Brindle must confirm that any revised off-block sequence remains compatible with the Departure Metering Service before the change is released to the airport community.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
